Terminology: paper round = 3 actions = engine turn; `round` in the context is the action slot 0..2.

rule_0_setup.description: Setup of a Dimension and of each player's deck. Tileset side depends on the player count (3x4 for up to 2 players, 4x4 for 3, 5x5 for 4 or more); every tile receives two face-down effects as traps and then one more card drawn from the shuffled monsters+skills pile. Each player draws 2 character cards and keeps 1, is dealt 10 effects and 4 skills (any of them may go to the archive instead of the deck), is dealt 2 class cards and keeps 1 (placed face up as the class permanent), then tops the deck up with A/B/M/P cards to at least 15 cards. Entry points are chosen in descending Will order; an entry tile may not hold a monster, may not be adjacent to a non-ally, and must be at least 2 tiles from any enemy; entering counts as a Move action (instants allowed) and the entry tile's traps still resolve. The engine evaluates these counts at turn 0 before the first action.

rule_1_actions_per_round.description: Turn economy. A character has exactly 3 actions per paper round (one engine turn), each chosen from Attack, Block, Move, Posture (or Empty Posture / Empty Move, Rule 6). A monster uses the action count printed on its card, 1 to 4; when an opponent has more actions than you, the surplus actions on your side are forced Empty Postures (and a forced EP may not be turned into an Empty Move). A player may delay entering the tileset and may cast permanents outside the Dimension so they are ready on the entry tile. The engine stores actions_per_round on every unit and derives the forced-EP count from the difference.

rule_2_discover_tile.description: Discovering a tile. A face-down tile turns face up ('open') the moment a unit Attacks it or Moves towards it. If a creature lies there it awakens (Rule 3) and the tile's effects become its hand. If only effects lie there the tile is a trap: every effect fires once against the discoverer with a power of 20 per element (pc ruling), i.e. trap power = 20 x number of trap elements; an element whose power does not exceed the defender's stat fails (Rule 18) and one failing element fails its whole effect (Rule 4). Context fields: tile.open, tile.creature, tile.effects (entry ids), tile.effect_elements (all elements of the trap effects).

rule_3_monster.description: Awakened creature behaviour. An awakened creature never leaves its tile (move distance 0) and attacks any enemy in contact (hex distance 1). All effects lying on its tile form its hand; its actions are rolled on D6 (Rule 5). While no enemy is in contact the creature regenerates. The creature is steered by the next enemy player in seating order (the player after the one in contact). Context: target is the creature (target.kind == 'creature', target.awake), dist the caster-creature distance.

rule_4_traps.description: Trap resolution. A trap (open tile with effects and no creature) is disabled once all of its effects have failed to kill or lock the discoverer: the discoverer survives the damage and is not locked. An effect fails as a whole as soon as one of its elements fails, i.e. when the trap power (20 per element, Rule 2) does not exceed the defender's stat behind that element. All traps resolve within one round. A kill or lock costs the character one re-entry attempt (a 'time'); the character may re-enter and fight for a draw.

rule_5_monster_dice.description: Monster actions by dice. A creature in contact with a character rolls 4 D6 per action (or its printed pattern such as BAAPM / AAAM, one die per letter) and acts on the colour that scores highest: green = Block, blue/white = Move, red = Attack, black = Posture. When Posture wins the creature picks an effect from its hand and stops rolling until all of that effect's elements are emitted (one per action). Context: caster is the creature, caster.dice_pattern its optional printed pattern, die_face the winning colour, cast.step/of the running emission.

rule_6_empty_posture_move.description: Empty Posture / Empty Move. EP is the no-op action: it gains no matrix edge (pc: 'EP no benefits'), may still emit an element, and always returns to the hand. The same card may be declared first as Empty Move: the unit advances halfway toward its target (ceil(dist/2) hexes). For the resolution matrix the enemy picks the empty type that hurts the empty actor: Attack treats EP as Posture (A vs EP = 2), Posture treats EP as Empty Move (P vs EP = 1), Block treats EM as Move (B vs EM = 1); Move/Block vs EP are neutral. A forced EP (Rule 1/7) may not be converted into EM. Reaver exception (pc): its EP and EM fight as Attack.

rule_7_turn_round_sequence.description: Turn structure. Units in contact commit their action cards face down simultaneously each action; cards flip, instants and skills may still be played, targets are pointed out and the resolution matrix applies: base 1 damage for Attack plus 1 per edge (A>P/EP, P>M/EM/EP, M>B, B>A), so A vs P = 2 and B vs A = 1 to the attacker. Effects are emitted only on P/EP. After the third action of the engine turn, characters may discard and draw up to 5 (Rule 10); monsters never discard. A unit facing an opponent with more actions per round fills the gap with forced Empty Postures.

rule_8_card_declare_sequence.description: Declaration order within an action: (1) Empty Move, (2) the action card (A/B/M/P/EP), (3) effects — a declared effect binds this action to emit its next element, (4) skills, instants, class abilities OR a point-buy against a token (Rule 24). There is no stack: everything applies, prohibitions are applied last as replacements. Pc override: instants are committed with the action; if the action's maths gave the player no benefit (took no less, dealt no more, healed no more than without the instant) the instant returns to the hand instead of being discarded, in bonus rounds too (rule_8_instant_returns). rule_9_class_card.description: Class card. On entering a Dimension the class card is in play as a permanent with a token of fixed value 6 per colour (no point-buy at placement). rule_10_draw.description: Draw. At the end of the engine turn (after action slot 2) a character draws until the hand holds 5 cards (hand_refill; Haste ∀ raises the limit by 1, Balefire draws 5 at once). rule_11_archive.description: Archive. Instead of discarding, a used card may be moved to the archive, but only while the cards still in circulation (deck + discard + hand + holding) stay at or above 15 afterwards (deck_floor; pc: the deck never goes below 15). Defeated creatures' cards also live in the archive and can be used by Summoning / Possess / Resurrect as outer-dimension allies: such an ally enters on its owner's tile, moves with the owner and is steered like a player-managed monster. An archived card may always be moved back to the discard pile. Context: caster.circulating_cards, card (entry id), card_kind.

rule_12_permanent_types.description: Permanents and tokens. A permanent card stays in front of the deck until destroyed; at placement the caster point-buys the emitted element: roll point_buy_dice_count(stat) d6, the roll fits when the sum is at most the stat (point_buy_succeeds), the highest die becomes the token value (point_buy_token_value); pc: a permanent may re-roll until the point-buy fits. A small neutral die over the permanent shows the lowest colour value. Token kinds: tile token (big coloured die right of the tile, bonus to every creature there), permanent token (coloured die over a stat, added), stat-penalty token (wooden die under a stat, subtracted), shield token (Rule 20). Context: card (effect id), dice (the roll), permanent.tokens.

rule_14.description: Rule 14 in three parts. A — acquisition/trade: effects and skills are acquired by conquering a tile or from a defeated character's deck and go to discard or archive; adjacent characters may trade archives for an action when one of them moves towards the other, and may discard into each other's piles. B — life: life = round_half_up(sum of stats / 10) (life_from_stats): every character has 40 -> 4, a Dragon 80 -> 8; the life die is recalculated whenever damage is taken or a token of value 5 or more is added to the tile or character. C — adjacency: a unit may only be attacked from the surrounding tiles (paper: 8 neighbours; engine: hex distance 1, in_contact).

rule_15_target_follow.description: Targeting. Attack and Move target one enemy or tile; Posture and Block are untargeted (pc), Block dealing 1 to each enemy who attacked you (B > A edge). Pc target priority when no explicit target: (1) the enemy against whom I take less damage, (2) an enemy that would take damage, (3) the enemy with the lowest life; a right-clicked target is honoured when in contact. Score = 100 x i_take_less + 10 x enemy_takes_damage - life, highest wins. Two units Moving to the same tile: only the one truly using Move arrives; on mirrored Moves nobody moves. An attacker may follow a target that moves away. Context: candidate.{i_take_less, damage_to_enemy, life}, caster.move_target, defender.move_target.

rule_17_skills.description: Skills as instants. rule_18_element_emit.description: Element emission. Each element of an effect is emitted with power equal to the caster's stat behind it (stat_of via elements.json: Vitality; World for souls/time/space; Matter for air/water/earth/fire; Will for concentration/harmony) and resisted with the defender's same stat. An element whose power does not exceed the defender's stat fails (deals 0 on that element; a non-damage effect is saved). Point-buy effects cannot be resisted. The current element is elements[cast.step]. Pc Counter Spell: one element type, subtract my stat from theirs per instance. Disabled elements (Disable) may not be emitted.

rule_19_effect_cast.description: Casting by contiguous Postures. A non-instant effect emits one element per Posture / Empty Posture, in the card's order; any other action between two emissions interrupts the cast (pc: the cast fails and the card is discarded), except that Move does not interrupt a class that may emit on Move (Monk). After casting the card is discarded unless it is a permanent (goes in front of the deck) or channeled (keeps going while the caster stays on the same tile). Context: cast.step/of, cast.origin_tile.

rule_20_effect_types.description: Effect types and the point-buy. Types (valid_effect_types): damage (Rule 21 stat comparison), point-buy (dice, unresistable), instant (any action), shield token (die over the tile as extra life, cumulative), channeling (temporary permanent, lost when channeling stops or its last token dies), stat buy (bank the stat per emission until the card's total, stat_buy_paid). Point-buy: roll point_buy_dice_count(stat) d6; the roll fits when the sum is at most the stat (point_buy_succeeds); keep the highest die (point_buy_token_value) as token or damage. Pc: the point-buy is per emission and a failed roll re-emits only that element next action; once a non-instant effect is picked only P/EP/EM remain selectable; Fireball deals delta damage and leaves a fire tile token; Force Shield is permanent and its Vitality die is subtracted from the effect sum. Context: dice (this roll), cast.non_instant_selected.

rule_21_effect_damage.description: Effect damage. For a completed damage effect, per element take max(caster stat - defender stat, 0), sum, divide by 10 and round half up (0.5 -> 1, 0.4 -> 0; resolved contradiction: not a ceiling): fire 3 + water 2 = 5 -> 1 damage; 2 + 2 = 4 -> 0. Damage applies when the defender has no tokens left to destroy; otherwise the defender chooses a token to lose instead. Pc Dodge: 1 less combat damage in total. Implemented as rule_21_delta_damage; life uses the same rounding (life_from_stats).

rule_24_destroy_permanent_token.description: Destroying permanents and tokens. Pc: on a Posture / Empty Posture the caster emits a stat (one point-buy of one of the token's elements) against the closest adjacent enemy's permanents; a die at least the token's power destroys it (using_rule_24); fixed-power permanents (class card, summons, golems, elementals, resurrect) need a 6 (fixed_power_6); the class card itself can never be destroyed.
